# Render

Managed application hosting with a free tier that does not require a credit card. Documented as the
winning backend host for [[stickfps]]'s game server after the transport swap in
[[websocket-tcp-over-geckos-udp]] — see [[render-over-fly-io]] for the decision itself, which
reversed a rejection made earlier in the same project.

## The two properties that decided it

**No public inbound UDP.** This is why Render was rejected the first time it was evaluated: a
UDP-over-WebRTC transport cannot be served from it at all. Once the transport became plain
WebSocket-over-TCP, the disqualifier disappeared. Render terminates TLS and proxies WebSocket
upgrades on the normal HTTP port, which is all [[ws-websocket-server]] needs.

**Free tier, no card.** The stated trigger for the whole change. Koyeb is recorded as an equal
alternative on the same criterion.

## How it is configured — dashboard, not file

The runbook is dashboard settings rather than a committed manifest: Root Directory `server`, build
`npm install && npm run build`, start `npm start`, health check `/healthz`. **There is no
`render.yaml` in the repository**, no CI, and no `.github/`.

This is the significant operational fact about the whole deployment: it is *written down* rather than
*declared in code*. A dashboard-configured service cannot be diffed, reviewed or recreated from the
repo — the runbook in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` is the only copy, and nothing verifies that it still
matches reality. The [[docker]] image in the tree is not what Render builds; it belongs to the
Fly.io path.

## Known trade-off

Free instances idle down after roughly 15 minutes without traffic, so the first player to arrive
waits for a cold start — and a game server holding a 60 Hz loop is not idle-friendly by nature.
